findings.evidence: It came out plain and sure, the way a thing does when it is right.
findings.diagnosis: The contract bars the customer from delivering tidy validation; this relocates that validation to the narrator, which pronounces the turn correct — the story congratulating its own compromise.

findings.evidence: "No's the easy one." Rennie shut the hose off. "I've a harder one, if you want it."
findings.diagnosis: The spec's purpose is to force Rennie's choice between the paid false launch and the true answer, but she is on the side of truth from the first tap; the false launch is never a live temptation, so the turn reads as a clever fix, not a moral choice.

findings.evidence: Under the big light the paint looked better than ever, which was the cruelty of paint.
findings.diagnosis: Opens on an interpretive abstraction instead of letting the image carry it.
